mostWorthwhile.text: Examining the 1801 constitution was most worthwhile: it showed how abolition could coexist with restrictions on workers’ choices without diminishing emancipation’s achievement.

leastWorthwhile.text: The first combination was straightforward and the only offered action, so it involved little decision-making, though its emphasis on insurgents’ agency mattered.

surprise.text: The constitution preserved abolition while requiring plantation cultivation, separating legal freedom from freedom to leave work.

arbitrary.text: No action felt purposeless; the combinations followed the chapter’s questions, although most choices were supplied as the only compatible option.

continue.text: I would continue: the chapter’s distinctions between emancipation, labour coercion and independence made me curious about their later consequences.
